coldOpen.title: Delhi, 1947
coldOpen.text: Your Dada leaves everything behind but one thing: a handwritten book of recipes.

coldOpen.title: Burns Road, Karachi
coldOpen.text: For forty years his thela is famous for chai and bun kabab. Then, one winter, it goes quiet.

coldOpen.title: Today
coldOpen.text: The thela is yours. Rs 25,000, a kettle and Dada's book. Burns Road is waking up.

steps.text: Assalam-o-alaikum, beta! I am Rasheed. Since 1975 I have had my chai at this spot. Your Dada made it better than anyone. Chalo, let us see what you can do.
First things first: nothing is on your board. Open the Menu.
Put chai on. Tap "Off the board" next to Doodh patti chai.
I will be your first customer. Watch the bar over my head: it turns gold while you cook. The cooking is automatic; running the business is your job.
Paisa in the galla! Every plate goes in here. You pay for stock, rent and wages from it at the end of the day.
Here come your first customers. Keep an eye on the line and on their patience bars.
The street has gone quiet. Shout "Aao bhai!" to pull in the people walking past.
"Mehenga hai!" Your Dada sold chai for Rs 80, beta. Open the Menu.
Bring chai down to Rs 80. The chip turns green at a fair price; "Pricey" means some people walk away.
Fair price. Watch the next customer smile.
Your milk is nearly finished! Open Supplies.
Every dawn the kiryana tops you up to this level. Raise milk to 60. Milk spoils overnight, so do not overdo it.
No need to wait for dawn: tap "Top up everything" and the corner shop sends it now.
Afternoons are slow on Burns Road. Speed up time until the evening.
Maghrib. The tube lights come on and the street fills up. This rush is yours, beta. I will be watching from my chair.
This is your hisaab. Sales minus stock, ghee, wages and rent. MUNAFA means profit; NUQSAN means loss. Your Dada stamped his book every night.

steps.title: Your first goal
steps.text: Serve 300 customers and earn Rs 75,000. Then the owner upstairs will let you set up a takhta on the pavement. The bar at the top of the screen shows how close you are.

walkout_tutorial.text: Someone got tired of waiting. It happens, beta; nothing is lost.

walkout.text: People are walking off before you serve them. A chhotu takes orders while you cook, so the line moves faster.

soldOut.text: Khatam! Something sold out. Raise its top-up level in Supplies so the dawn delivery brings more.

tooExpensive.text: "Mehenga hai!" A "Pricey" chip on the Menu means some people walk away.

queueFull.text: The line got so long that people walked past. Serve faster before you shout again.

outage.text: Load shedding. Everything is slower in the dark. Once you have the dhaba, a generator keeps you going.

loss.text: A loss today. Look at the Kharcha side: stock that spoils and idle wages eat the galla. In Act 1 I will always lend you enough for tomorrow's stock.

noShout.text: Three days and not one "Aao bhai"! A shout pulls in people walking past. Use it when the street is busy.

noPrice.text: Prices are not carved in stone. As your Shohrat grows, people happily pay more. Try it on the Menu.

Staff.title: Staff
Staff.text: Chhotu can take orders while you cook. The line moves faster and people wait longer. He costs a daily wage, so hire him when you are busy.

Shop.title: The Shop
Shop.text: Your thela can do more, beta. The Shop sells upgrades you can see on the cart: stools, a bigger kettle, tube lights, a painted signboard. After Act 1 the pavement dhaba is set up here too.

Store.title: The Store
Store.text: Dada's trunk and other extras are in the Store. Nothing in it is needed to finish the game.

fat.title: Desi ghee or oil?
fat.text: Now that you run a dhaba, the choice is yours. Ghee tastes better and builds Asli-pan; oil costs less per plate. People notice the difference.

kitaab.title: Patience
kitaab.text: The bar over each head is a customer's patience. It turns gold while their order cooks. Empty bars walk away.

kitaab.title: The galla
kitaab.text: Every sale goes into the galla. Stock, rent and wages come out of it at the end of the day.

kitaab.title: Aao bhai!
kitaab.text: The shout pulls in people walking past for a while, then needs time to recharge. Use it when the street is busy and your line is short.

kitaab.title: Prices
kitaab.text: The chip on each dish says how people see the price. Fair is safe; Pricey loses some customers; Too pricey loses many. Fame and Asli-pan let you charge more.

kitaab.title: Supplies
kitaab.text: The kiryana and the qasai deliver at dawn up to your top-up levels. Milk, dahi and meat spoil overnight, so buy what a day needs.

kitaab.title: Time
kitaab.text: Mornings (nashta) and evenings are busy; afternoons are slow and Juma brings a lull. Speed up the quiet hours.

kitaab.title: The hisaab
kitaab.text: At night the ledger shows sales against stock, ghee, wages and rent. MUNAFA is profit, NUQSAN is loss.

kitaab.title: Staff
kitaab.text: A chhotu speeds up orders and keeps people patient. At the dhaba a karigar cooks nihari. Wages are paid every night.

kitaab.title: Ghee or oil
kitaab.text: Desi ghee tastes better and builds Asli-pan. Oil is cheaper per plate but people can tell.

kitaab.title: Load shedding
kitaab.text: Power cuts slow the kitchen and thin the street. A generator at the dhaba keeps things running, for the price of its fuel.

kitaab.title: Aaj ka kaam
kitaab.text: Every day brings three small goals. Each one pays cash and a few silver coins the moment it is done. Tap the goal bar to see them.

kitaab.title: Rush streak
kitaab.text: Serve customers in a row without anyone walking off and the Rush streak grows. Happy customers tip more during a streak; one walkout resets it.

kitaab.title: Upgrades
kitaab.text: The Shop sells upgrades for the thela. Each one shows on the cart and helps for good: stools for patience, a bigger kettle for chai, tube lights for the night crowd.

kitaab.title: Act 1
kitaab.text: Serve 300 customers and earn Rs 75,000 to set up the pavement dhaba. In Act 1 the game never ends: Uncle Rasheed lends you enough for tomorrow's stock.
